page: Microsoft Azure F64-32amds_v7 is a compute-focused and memory-intensive virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz. Configured with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs without multithreading (1 thread per core), the instance integrates 512.0 GB of system memory, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include AVX-512 extensions (such as AVX-512 VNNI and BF16) and 7559 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. The platform contains no discrete graphics accelerators.

Benchmark outcomes show top-tier single-core performance alongside strong multi-core scalability. Stress-ng single-core tests place in the top 10% (score 3642.79), complemented by strong gzip compression (39.65 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (17.84 GB/sec). Memory architecture tests demonstrate high throughput, recording 219.58 GB/sec in large-block uncached reads and a top-10% PassMark memory score of 3029.38. Database evaluation shows exceptional throughput, with PassMark database operations reaching 37989.46 (top 10%) and Redis SET handling 93.4 million operations per second.

With its 1:16 core-to-memory ratio and 7.5 TB NVMe disk space, the hardware profile offers substantial density for in-memory workloads and high-throughput I/O pipelines without paying for specialized GPU hardware. CPU-driven LLM inference performs in the top tier for small 135M parameter models (5006.15 tokens/sec prompt, 395.18 tokens/sec generation), but decreases to mid-range performance on large 70B models due to the absence of dedicated accelerators.

The F64-32amds_v7 is particularly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-speed data compression pipelines, and CPU-bound analytical data processing where dedicated non-threaded cores and expansive local NVMe disk arrays are essential.

In benchmarks, the server excels in single-core compute (top 10% in stress-ng and data decompression), PassMark database operations (37989.46), and memory bandwidth, while achieving 93.4 million Redis SET operations per second. CPU-based small LLM inference also reaches top-tier throughput. Offering massive fast local storage and memory density, the instance provides high qualitative efficiency for non-GPU computational tasks.
